job.title: Anthropic Fellows Program, AI Safety & Security

strengths: Research on trustworthy and explainable AI, LLM-as-a-judge
Experience evaluating and mitigating hallucinations in clinical text summarisation
Teaching and coordinating academic projects, including Erasmus and international collaborations

cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am a PhD candidate in Computer Engineering focusing on hybrid evaluation metrics for Turkish text summarisation. My recent work on LLM‑as‑a‑judge and on trustworthy, explainable AI directly aligns with Anthropic's goal of safe and interpretable systems. At Yozgat Bozok University I lead the Computer Technologies Department and coordinate international academic activities, which has honed my ability to move quickly, work collaboratively, and communicate results clearly.

During my MSc I built evaluation tools for automatic summarisation, and my current research extends these tools to assess hallucinations in clinical texts. This experience gives me a solid grounding in empirical AI research and the practical skills needed to produce public outputs such as papers. My background as a software engineer before 2019 means I am fluent in Python and comfortable with rapid prototyping.

I am motivated to apply my expertise to AI safety and to learn from Anthropic's mentors. The fellowship's focus on fast‑paced, full‑time research matches my desire to transition into a dedicated research role.

Thank you for considering my application.

Best regards,
Anıl Kuş
short_pitch: I research trustworthy AI and LLM evaluation, and I can deliver empirical results quickly.

answers.why_this_role: I want to apply my expertise in LLM evaluation and hallucination mitigation to concrete AI safety problems, and the fellowship offers the focused, full‑time environment I need.
answers.why_this_organisation: Anthropic's mission to build safe, interpretable AI matches my research interests in trustworthy systems and aligns with my commitment to societal benefit.
answers.relevant_experience: My PhD work on hybrid metrics for summarisation, research on LLM‑as‑a‑judge, and projects on explainable AI give me hands‑on experience with the kinds of empirical studies the fellowship expects.
answers.research_interests: I am interested in evaluating AI outputs for safety, reducing hallucinations in specialised domains, and developing metrics that make LLM behaviour transparent.
answers.additional_information: I have coordinated international academic programmes, co‑founded a tech centre, and hold two patents, demonstrating leadership and innovation.
